newsitem.title: LEBANON: Byblos Bank gives details of $50-mln Euronote.
newsitem.headline: Byblos Bank gives details of $50-mln Euronote.

text.p: Beirut's Byblos Bank said on Thursday its $50 million three-year Euronote issue will be priced at minimum of 2.75 percent per year over three-year U.S. treasuries as at September 9, 1996.
The bank, one of Lebanon's biggest, said in a newspaper advertisement that interest will be payable twice yearly on March 23 and September 23.
Three classes of paper will be issued: A notes in denominations of $1,000, B notes of $10,000 each and C notes in denominations of $100,000. All notes mature on September 23, 1999.
SBC Warburg and Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest SAL, who are managing the issue, said last week that the notes would be listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.

The issue will make the fast-growing Byblos Bank the second Beirut bank to enter into the Eurobond market after a trailblazing $60 million bond issue in June by Credit Libanais, lead managed by Merrill Lynch International.
